Microelements (trace elements) are needed by plants in very small quantities. Examples include: iron (Fe), manganese (Mn), boron (B), zinc (Zn), copper (Cu). The macroelements (needed in large quantities) are N, P, K, Ca, Mg, S. The correct answer is C (the trace element listed).

Hydrophytes (aquatic plants) adaptations include: air spaces (aerenchyma) for buoyancy, thin cuticle, stomata on upper surface, large leaf surface area. Thick waxy cuticle is a xerophyte (desert plant) adaptation — NOT a hydrophyte adaptation. The correct answer is C (thick waxy cuticle).

Cell theory was formulated by Schleiden (1838, plants), Schwann (1839, animals), and Virchow (1855, cells from cells). Watson and Crick (DNA structure) did NOT contribute to cell theory. The correct answer is A (the scientist who did not contribute).

The malaria parasite (Plasmodium) is transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito. The female bites to obtain blood meals needed for egg development, thereby transmitting Plasmodium sporozoites. The correct answer is A (female Anopheles mosquito).

Deamination is the process by which excess amino acids are broken down — the amino group (NH₂) is removed, producing ammonia which is converted to urea in the liver. The carbon skeleton is used for energy. The correct answer is A (deamination).

Benefits of conservation include: sustainable resource use, preservation of biodiversity, maintenance of ecosystem services, and future resource availability. Pollution of water bodies is a harmful activity, NOT a benefit of conservation. The correct answer is C (pollution/harmful activity).
Plants that store food in their roots include: cassava (starch in tuberous roots), carrot, yam, radish. These storage organs are modified roots. The correct answer is A (cassava/the example shown).

The theory of inheritance of acquired characteristics through use and disuse was propounded by Jean-Baptiste Lamarck (Lamarckism). Darwin proposed natural selection, not acquired inheritance. The correct answer is D (Lamarck).

The toad's long, sticky, rapid tongue is an adaptation for catching insects — it shoots out quickly to catch prey and the sticky surface traps the insect. The correct answer is A (catching insects/prey capture).
Auxin (produced at the apical meristem/tip) inhibits the development of lateral buds — this is called apical dominance. When the apex is removed, lateral buds grow. The correct answer is B (auxin).
A cell capable of independent (self) existence is a unicellular organism (e.g., Amoeba, Paramecium). These perform all life functions in a single cell. The correct answer is A (unicellular organism).

Translocation is the movement of food (dissolved sugars, amino acids) in soluble form through the phloem vessels to all parts of the plant. This is bidirectional (up and down). The correct answer is D (translocation).

Phloem tissue carries organic food (sugars produced during photosynthesis) from the site of production (leaves) to all other parts of the plant — this process is called translocation. The correct answer is C (phloem).

A test cross (back cross) is used to determine the genotype of an organism showing the dominant phenotype — it is crossed with a homozygous recessive individual. If any offspring show the recessive phenotype, the organism is heterozygous. The correct answer is A (determine the genotype of a dominant phenotype organism).

Soil fertility conservation methods include: crop rotation, adding manure/compost, mulching, contour ploughing. Monoculture (growing the same crop repeatedly) depletes soil nutrients and does NOT conserve fertility. The correct answer is A (monoculture/the practice that depletes fertility).
In Euglena, the contractile vacuole regulates water balance — it collects excess water and contracts to expel it through the reservoir. The correct answer is C (contractile vacuole).

Nigeria's biomes include: tropical rainforest (south), Guinea savanna (middle belt), Sudan savanna (north), Sahel savanna (far north), and mangrove swamp (Niger Delta). The correct answer is D (tropical rainforest, savanna, mangrove, and Sahel).

Fresh water habitats (rivers, lakes, ponds) are characterised by: low salt concentration, constant temperature fluctuations, varied light penetration, flowing or still water. High salinity is characteristic of marine/saltwater habitats — NOT freshwater. The correct answer is A (high salinity).

A test cross in genetics is used to determine the genotype of an individual showing the dominant phenotype — whether it is homozygous dominant (AA) or heterozygous (Aa). The correct answer is C (determine genotype).
A community is a group of interacting populations (different species) living together in a particular habitat. It includes all living organisms in an area. The correct answer is C (community).

Iron is required by plants mainly for chlorophyll formation — though iron is not part of the chlorophyll molecule itself, it is essential for chlorophyll synthesis. Iron deficiency causes chlorosis (yellowing). The correct answer is A (chlorophyll formation).

Primary producers are autotrophs that produce organic matter from inorganic materials via photosynthesis. Green plants (e.g., grass, algae) are the primary producers in food chains. The correct answer is A (green plant/grass).

The incomplete breakdown of glucose into alcohol (ethanol), carbon dioxide, and energy (ATP) under anaerobic conditions is called anaerobic respiration or fermentation. This occurs in yeast and in waterlogged plant roots. The correct answer is C (fermentation/anaerobic respiration).

Succulent plants (cacti, desert plants) store water in their thick stems and leaves — an adaptation to survive long dry periods in arid environments. This is a xerophytic adaptation. The correct answer is A (xerophytes/desert plants).

During inhalation, the external intercostal muscles contract, raising the ribs upward and outward. This is caused by muscle contraction (an active process). The process is best described as muscle contraction. The correct answer is D (contraction of intercostal muscles).

Before blood transfusion, blood typing (ABO and Rhesus grouping) is essential to ensure compatibility and prevent haemolytic reactions. The donor's blood must be compatible with the recipient's. The correct answer is C (blood typing/compatibility testing).

In Paramecium, the oral groove collects food particles. In Euglena, the flagellum (which also creates water currents and aids food collection near the reservoir) performs a similar function. The correct answer is D (flagellum).
Fossils are the remains, impressions, or traces of animals and plants preserved in rocks over millions of years. They provide evidence for organic evolution. The correct answer is B (fossils).

Processes releasing CO₂: respiration, combustion, decomposition. Photosynthesis absorbs CO₂ rather than releasing it — it is the process that will NOT release carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. The correct answer is C (photosynthesis).

An inflorescence is a complete flowering shoot — a cluster of flowers arranged on a stem (floral axis). It is a branched system bearing multiple flowers, not a single flower. The correct answer is B (a cluster/system of flowers on a stem).

Bacteria that derive energy for food synthesis by oxidising inorganic compounds (e.g., sulphur, nitrogen, iron) are called chemoautotrophs — they use chemical energy rather than light energy. The correct answer is A (chemoautotrophs).

In a hypertonic solution (more concentrated than the cell), water leaves the plant cell by osmosis, causing the cell membrane to shrink away from the cell wall — this is called plasmolysis. The correct answer is B (plasmolysis).

Sex-linked diseases are caused by genes on the sex chromosomes (usually X chromosome). Colour blindness is a classic example of an X-linked recessive condition. The correct answer is A (colour blindness).

Mammals are homeothermic (warm-blooded) — they maintain a constant internal body temperature regardless of external temperature changes, through metabolic processes. The correct answer is D (constant internal temperature regulation).

Supporting tissues in plants include: xylem (lignified), sclerenchyma (fibres, stone cells), and collenchyma. Parenchyma is a basic packing tissue, NOT a supporting tissue — it is thin-walled and lacks lignification for support. The correct answer is B (parenchyma).

The chloroplast is the organelle responsible for photosynthesis — it contains chlorophyll and the enzymes for the light reactions (thylakoids) and dark reactions (stroma). The correct answer is B (chloroplast).

Meiosis and mitosis similarities: both involve DNA replication, both produce cells, both have similar phases. The key difference — meiosis produces 4 haploid cells while mitosis produces 2 diploid cells. The NOT true statement about both is D (the difference).

Reproduction in plants includes: vegetative propagation, budding, spore formation, seed formation. Photosynthesis is a metabolic process for food production — it is NOT a form of reproduction. The correct answer is A (photosynthesis).
Mitosis produces 2 daughter cells (genetically identical to the parent cell and to each other) with the same chromosome number as the parent. The correct answer is A (2 daughter cells).

Competition between members of the SAME population (same species) over limited resources is called intraspecific competition — it is the most intense form of competition because they need identical resources. The correct answer is C (intraspecific competition).

Inherited characteristics in humans: eye colour, blood group, hair texture, skin colour. Language/education is acquired through environment and experience — it is NOT inherited genetically. The correct answer is D (language/education).

In the nucleus, chromosomes are the thread-like structures (made of DNA and protein/histone) in which genes are embedded. Genes are located at specific positions (loci) on chromosomes. The correct answer is B (chromosomes).

An exoskeleton is an external supporting structure. Examples include: chitin exoskeleton of insects (shell of beetles), shells of crabs and lobsters. The correct answer is C (insect exoskeleton/shell).

The hypothalamus produces releasing hormones that control the pituitary gland. It also produces ADH (antidiuretic hormone) and oxytocin, which are stored in the posterior pituitary. The correct answer is B (ADH and oxytocin / releasing hormones).
Oxygenated blood from the lungs returns to the heart via the pulmonary veins — these carry oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium of the heart. The correct answer is C (pulmonary veins).

Guinea worm (Dracunculus medinensis) lives in human tissues — this relationship where one organism (parasite) benefits at the expense of the other (host) is called parasitism. The correct answer is B (parasitism).

Reddish or purplish leaves in plants indicate phosphorus deficiency — phosphorus is needed for energy transfer (ATP) and nucleic acid synthesis. Without it, anthocyanin pigments accumulate causing red coloration. The correct answer is D (phosphorus).

The process by which organisms oxidise inorganic compounds to obtain energy (without light) is called chemosynthesis or chemoautotrophy. Nitrifying bacteria (Nitrosomonas, Nitrobacter) are examples. The correct answer is C (chemosynthesis).

Major groups of the plant kingdom include: Thallophyta, Bryophyta, Pteridophyta, Gymnosperms, Angiosperms. Fungi used to be classified as plants but are now a separate kingdom — they are NOT part of the plant kingdom. The correct answer is B (fungi).

True facts about enzymes: protein in nature, specific in action, denatured by high temperatures, lowered activation energy. The NOT true statement is B — enzymes are NOT consumed or permanently changed in reactions.

Dental formula i 2/2, c 1/1, pm 2/2, m 3/3 — 2 upper and 2 lower incisors, 1 canine each side, 2 premolars, 3 molars. This pattern with small canines and many premolars/molars is characteristic of a rabbit (herbivore with gnawing incisors). The correct answer is C (rabbit).
Earthworms excrete nitrogenous waste through nephridia (nephridium singular) — paired tubular excretory organs that remove waste from the coelomic fluid. The correct answer is D (nephridia).

The biosphere is the part of the earth (and atmosphere) where living organisms exist — encompassing all ecosystems on earth. It includes land (lithosphere), water (hydrosphere), and lower atmosphere where life exists. The correct answer is D (part of the earth and atmosphere where living organisms exist).
In a bee colony, the queen bee is the only female that lays eggs (fertilised eggs become worker bees or queens; unfertilised eggs become drones). The correct answer is D (queen bee).
Sun rays (solar energy/radiation) reach the earth's surface by radiation — electromagnetic radiation travels through the vacuum of space. No medium is required. The correct answer is C (radiation).
Translocation of food substances (sugars, amino acids) in plants takes place through the phloem — specifically through sieve tube elements. The correct answer is C (phloem).

Herbicides are chemicals used specifically to kill or control weeds (unwanted plants/herbs) that compete with crops. They are selective or non-selective weed killers. The correct answer is D (kill weeds).

Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting — it is required for the synthesis of clotting factors (prothrombin, factors VII, IX, X). Deficiency leads to impaired blood clotting and excessive bleeding. The correct answer is D (impaired blood clotting/excessive bleeding).

Effects of food shortage on population: increased mortality, decreased birth rate, emigration, disease. Increased population growth is NOT an effect of food shortage — food shortage limits population growth. The correct answer is D (increased population growth).
An anemometer is the instrument used to measure wind speed. It consists of rotating cups; faster rotation indicates higher wind speed. The correct answer is A (anemometer).
Glucose is the immediate (direct) source of energy to the body — it is broken down in cellular respiration to release ATP energy. The correct answer is D (glucose).

Plant hormones (phytohormones) include: auxins, gibberellins, cytokinins, abscisic acid (ABA), and ethylene. Insulin is an animal hormone (produced by the pancreas) — it is NOT a plant hormone. The correct answer is D (insulin).

Starch is the direct product of photosynthesis in leaves. Testing a leaf with iodine solution confirms photosynthesis — the leaf turns blue-black in areas that have photosynthesised (starch is present). The correct answer is D (starch).

Primary consumers eat producers (plants) directly. In a food chain, the organism feeding directly on plants is the primary consumer. The correct answer is B (the herbivore/primary consumer in the diagram).

Autecology is the study of the interrelationship of a single species (individual organism) with its environment. Synecology studies communities. The correct answer is B (a single species/organism and its environment).

Euglena possesses both plant characteristics (chloroplasts for photosynthesis) and animal characteristics (moves with flagellum, can ingest food in darkness). It is therefore classified as having both plant and animal characteristics. The correct answer is B (Euglena).
The tip of the tongue is sensitive to sweet tastes. The tongue has taste zones: tip (sweet), sides (salty/sour), back (bitter). The correct answer is C (sweet).

Enzyme activity is affected by: temperature, pH, substrate concentration, enzyme concentration, and presence of inhibitors. All of these are factors. The correct answer is D (all of the above / temperature, pH, and substrate concentration).

Thrombocytes (platelets) are cell fragments responsible for blood clotting — they aggregate at wound sites and release clotting factors that initiate the coagulation cascade. The correct answer is A (blood clotting).

The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) — a network of membranous channels — is responsible for transporting substances within the cell. Rough ER transports proteins; smooth ER transports lipids. The correct answer is C (endoplasmic reticulum).
Liver diseases include: hepatitis (A, B, C), cirrhosis, and liver cancer. The correct answer is C (hepatitis — a liver disease).

Excretory organs include: kidneys, lungs, skin, liver. The spleen is NOT an excretory organ — it filters and recycles old red blood cells and is part of the immune system. The correct answer is A (spleen).

Insects breathe through spiracles — small openings on the thorax and abdomen that lead to a network of air tubes called tracheae. Air diffuses directly to tissues through this tracheal system. The correct answer is E (spiracles and tracheae).

Dilute hydrochloric acid (HCl) in the stomach: activates pepsinogen to pepsin, kills bacteria, provides acidic medium. HCl does NOT digest carbohydrates — that is done by amylase in the mouth/pancreas. The correct answer is C (digest carbohydrates).
A flower with one carpel (simple pistil) is called monocarpellary. The single carpel contains the ovary, style, and stigma. The correct answer is B (monocarpellary).

A potometer measures the rate of water uptake by a cut shoot, which approximates the rate of transpiration. It consists of a calibrated capillary tube attached to the shoot. The correct answer is D (potometer).
Chromosomes are found in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells. They are thread-like structures made of DNA and histone proteins that carry genetic information. The correct answer is D (nucleus).

Cassava mosaic disease causes stunted growth and reduced yield in cassava plants. It is caused by the African cassava mosaic virus (ACMV), transmitted by whiteflies. The correct answer is D (cassava mosaic virus/disease).
A population is the total number of individuals of the same species living in a defined area at a given time. The correct answer is D (individuals of the same species in a defined area).

Functions of mammalian skin: protection, temperature regulation, excretion (sweat), vitamin D synthesis, sensory reception. Haemopoiesis (blood cell production) occurs in bone marrow — NOT in the skin. The correct answer is A (haemopoiesis/blood cell production).
Mealy bugs (Pseudococcidae) are common pests of cocoa, cassava, citrus, and ornamental plants. They suck plant sap and transmit diseases. The correct answer is A (cocoa/the crop mentioned).

Blood groups (ABO, Rh) and tongue rolling (can/cannot roll) are examples of discontinuous variation — they fall into distinct categories with no intermediate forms. The correct answer is B (discontinuous variation).

Reflex actions are controlled by the spinal cord (for spinal reflexes) via reflex arcs. The brain is not involved in the initial reflex response (though it receives information afterwards). The correct answer is C (spinal cord).

The removal of undigested food substances from the body is called egestion (defecation) — the elimination of faeces through the anus. This is different from excretion (removal of metabolic waste). The correct answer is B (egestion).

The correct sequence of energy transfer in an ecosystem: Producers (plants) → Primary consumers (herbivores) → Secondary consumers (carnivores) → Tertiary consumers (top predators). The correct answer is D (sun → producers → consumers).
Xylem tissue consists of: xylem vessels, tracheids, xylem parenchyma, and xylem fibres. Sieve tube elements belong to PHLOEM tissue, not xylem. The correct answer is A (sieve tube elements).

Characteristics of digestive enzymes: they are protein in nature, specific, work in specific pH, denatured by heat. The NOT characteristic statement is B — enzymes are not changed/consumed in the reaction.

Simple sugars (monosaccharides) are also called monosaccharides — the simplest form of carbohydrate that cannot be hydrolysed further. Examples: glucose, fructose, galactose. The correct answer is C (monosaccharides).

Plant cells differ from animal cells by having: a rigid cell wall (cellulose), chloroplasts (for photosynthesis), a large central vacuole, and no centrioles. The correct answer is A (cell wall and chloroplasts).

Ultra-filtration (glomerular filtration) takes place in the Bowman's capsule — high blood pressure forces small molecules from the glomerular capillaries into the Bowman's capsule to form the glomerular filtrate. The correct answer is A (Bowman's capsule).

Incomplete combustion of petrol/diesel in car engines releases carbon monoxide (CO) — a toxic, colourless, odourless gas that binds to haemoglobin more readily than oxygen, causing carbon monoxide poisoning. The correct answer is B (carbon monoxide).

Glomerular filtrate contains: water, glucose, urea, mineral salts, amino acids. Plasma proteins (large molecules) cannot pass through the glomerular membrane — they are retained in the blood. The correct answer is A (plasma proteins).

Soil factors in an ecosystem (water content, mineral composition, texture, pH, temperature) are referred to as edaphic factors — from the Greek 'edaphos' meaning soil. The correct answer is C (edaphic factors).

Factors affecting photosynthesis: light intensity, CO₂ concentration, water availability, temperature, chlorophyll content. Wind speed does NOT directly affect photosynthesis (though it affects transpiration). The correct answer is C (wind speed).
Mycelium is the vegetative body of fungi — a network of thread-like hyphae that forms the main growth structure of fungi such as mushrooms, moulds, and other fungi. The correct answer is C (fungi).
Under-secretion (deficiency) of thyroxine before maturity causes cretinism — characterised by stunted growth, mental retardation, and low metabolic rate. The correct answer is A (cretinism).

In savanna trees, thick corky bark is an adaptation for protection against fires — the cork insulates the living tissue beneath from the heat of grass fires that occur during the dry season. The correct answer is B (protection against fire).
Ptyalin (salivary amylase) acts in the mouth — it begins carbohydrate digestion by breaking down starch into maltose in the slightly alkaline/neutral saliva (pH ~7). The correct answer is B (mouth).
The liver deaminates excess amino acids — removing the amino group (NH₂) to produce ammonia, which is then converted to urea for excretion. The correct answer is D (liver).

Vertebrates have a vertebral column (backbone). All fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals are vertebrates. Insects (Arthropoda) are invertebrates — they do NOT have a backbone. The correct answer is C (insect).

Exchange of materials (oxygen, CO₂, nutrients, wastes) between blood and tissues occurs in capillaries — they have walls only one cell thick, allowing easy diffusion. The correct answer is C (capillaries).
When ovules are arranged along the walls (sides) of the ovary cavity, this is called parietal placentation. The correct answer is D (parietal placentation).
Cotton (Gossypium spp.) is an industrial/fibre crop grown for its lint (used in textiles). The correct answer is A (industrial/fibre crop).

The tricuspid valve (right atrioventricular valve) is located between the right atrium and right ventricle. It has three cusps and prevents backflow of blood into the right atrium during ventricular contraction. The correct answer is D (right atrium and right ventricle).

The three main fingerprint patterns are: loops, whorls, and arches. There is no such fingerprint type called 'circles' — that is not a recognised fingerprint category. The correct answer is D (circles).
Pepsin (a protease) requires an acidic medium to function — it is activated in the stomach by hydrochloric acid and works optimally at pH ~2. The correct answer is D (pepsin).

Gametes (sex cells: sperm and eggs) are haploid — they contain half the normal chromosome number. The haploid number is represented as 'n'. So the number of chromosomes in a gamete is represented by n. The correct answer is A (n).

Denitrification is the process that reduces nitrogen content of soil — denitrifying bacteria (Pseudomonas denitrificans) convert nitrates back to nitrogen gas, which is released into the atmosphere. The correct answer is B (denitrification).

A pyramid of energy shows the amount of energy available at each trophic level in an ecosystem — it always has the largest base (most energy) at the producer level and decreases upward, reflecting 10% energy transfer efficiency. The correct answer is A (total energy available at each trophic level).

Calcium is essential for bone and teeth mineralisation. Deficiency of calcium (and vitamin D) in a child's diet causes rickets — characterised by soft, weak, deformed bones and bowed legs. The correct answer is D (rickets).

A climax community is established when ecological succession reaches a stable, self-perpetuating state — the community remains relatively unchanged unless disturbed. The correct answer is A (when the community is stable and self-sustaining).

Nitrifying bacteria convert ammonia to nitrites/nitrates (nitrification). Nitrosomonas converts NH₃ to NO₂⁻; Nitrobacter converts NO₂⁻ to NO₃⁻. The correct answer is C (Nitrobacter / the nitrifying bacterium).

The direct photosynthetic product is glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) — formed during the Calvin cycle (dark reactions) from CO₂, water, and light energy. Starch is a secondary storage product. The correct answer is B (glucose).

Veins carry deoxygenated blood (except pulmonary veins), have thin walls, large lumens, contain valves, and operate under low pressure. The NOT correct statement is C — veins do NOT have thick muscular walls (that is arteries). The correct answer is C.
Wind speed is measured with an anemometer — a device with rotating cups that spins proportionally to wind speed. The correct answer is A (anemometer).

During photosynthesis: light is absorbed, water is split (photolysis), CO₂ is fixed, glucose is synthesised, and oxygen is released. Glucose is oxidised during RESPIRATION — it does NOT occur during photosynthesis. The correct answer is A (oxidation of glucose).
RNA contains the bases: Adenine, Guanine, Cytosine, and Uracil. RNA does NOT contain Thymine — thymine is found only in DNA. The correct answer is D (thymine).

Poor growth and yellowing (chlorosis) of leaves is caused by nitrogen deficiency — nitrogen is needed for protein synthesis and chlorophyll production. Without nitrogen, leaves turn yellow. The correct answer is D (nitrogen).

Desert plant (xerophyte) structural adaptations for water conservation: sunken stomata, thick waxy cuticle, reduced leaf area, spines, succulent stems. Large leaf surface area increases water loss — it is NOT an adaptation for water conservation. The correct answer is A (large leaf surface area).

Evidence for organic evolution includes: fossil records, comparative anatomy, vestigial organs, embryology, biochemical similarities, and geographical distribution. Special creation (creationism) is NOT evidence of organic evolution — it opposes evolutionary theory. The correct answer is E (special creation).

Growing more than one type of crop on the same plot of land at the same time is called mixed cropping (or intercropping). It improves land use efficiency and reduces pest damage. The correct answer is C (mixed cropping).
CO₂ is removed from the atmosphere by photosynthesis — plants absorb CO₂ and fix it into organic compounds (glucose) using light energy. The correct answer is C (photosynthesis).

Heterotrophic nutrition modes include: holozoic (eating solid food), saprophytic (decomposing dead matter), parasitic (living on host). Photosynthesis is an AUTOTROPHIC mode — it is NOT heterotrophic. The correct answer is B (photosynthesis).

Glucagon is a hormone that raises blood glucose levels by stimulating glycogen breakdown in the liver. It is secreted by the alpha cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas. The correct answer is C (pancreas).

Blood carrying digested food (glucose, amino acids) from the small intestine flows into the liver via the hepatic portal vein — a unique vessel that delivers absorbed nutrients directly to the liver for processing. The correct answer is A (hepatic portal vein).

A caryopsis is a dry, indehiscent fruit where the seed coat is fused to the fruit wall (pericarp). It is characteristic of grasses — maize (corn) grain is a classic example of a caryopsis. The correct answer is C (maize).

Plant growth is influenced by: light, hormones (auxins, gibberellins, cytokinins), temperature, water, minerals. Colour of light affects plant responses, but the colour of the flower petals does NOT influence plant growth. The correct answer is D (flower colour).

In the Benedict's test for reducing sugars, the food substance is warmed with Benedict's reagent (blue) — if reducing sugars (glucose, maltose, fructose) are present, the solution turns from blue to green, yellow, orange, or brick-red. The correct answer is A (Benedict's reagent/solution).

Supporting tissues in plants include: sclerenchyma (fibres and stone cells), collenchyma, and xylem (lignified). Parenchyma is a storage/packing tissue — it is NOT a supporting tissue. The correct answer is A (parenchyma).

A tapeworm lives inside its host (mammal), deriving nutrition while harming the host — this one-sided relationship where one benefits (tapeworm) and the other is harmed (mammal) is called parasitism. The correct answer is B (parasitism).

The vitreous humour (jelly-like substance filling the eye behind the lens) helps maintain the shape of the eyeball and assists in focusing (refraction) of objects onto the retina. The correct answer is D (maintaining shape and focusing).

Water is the medium of transportation in higher plants — it dissolves and transports mineral salts through xylem (upward) and organic substances through phloem (translocation). The correct answer is A (water).

In mammals, fertilisation (fusion of sperm and egg) takes place in the Fallopian tube (oviduct) — specifically in the upper third (ampulla) of the fallopian tube. The correct answer is B (fallopian tube/oviduct).

Hearing involves: the pinna (collects sound), tympanic membrane (vibrates), ossicles (amplify), cochlea (converts to nerve impulses). The semicircular canals are involved in BALANCE, NOT hearing. The correct answer is D (semicircular canals).
Anabolic processes build up complex molecules from simpler ones (require energy). Photosynthesis (building glucose from CO₂ and water) is anabolic. The correct answer is D (photosynthesis).

Homeothermic (warm-blooded) organisms maintain a fairly constant body temperature regardless of external temperature. Birds and mammals are homeothermic. The correct answer is A (the mammal/bird shown).
An organism with identical allelic genes for a particular trait (both alleles the same, e.g., AA or aa) is described as homozygous. The correct answer is C (homozygous).

Reflex action involves: receptor → sensory neuron → relay neuron (in spinal cord) → motor neuron → effector. The cerebral cortex (brain) is NOT involved in the basic reflex arc — reflexes bypass conscious brain control. The correct answer is A (cerebral cortex).
Kidney diseases include: nephritis, kidney stones, renal failure. Hepatitis is a LIVER disease, not a kidney disease. The correct answer is B (hepatitis).
Dental formula i 3/3, c 1/1, pm 4/4, m 2/3 — large canines, multiple premolars, 3 lower molars. Multiple large canines and premolars suggest a carnivore. The correct answer is B (dog/carnivore).

Throwing down a hot pot quickly without thinking is a reflex action — a rapid, involuntary response to a stimulus (heat/pain) that is controlled by the spinal cord without conscious brain involvement. The correct answer is C (reflex action).
Animal cells lack: cell wall (cellulose), chloroplasts, and large central vacuole. These are plant cell structures. The correct answer is A (cell wall/chloroplast — not found in animal cell).

Ecological succession involves: colonisation by pioneer species, species replacement, increasing complexity, and ending in a climax community. Climax community reverting to pioneer stage does NOT occur in normal succession — it is associated with succession. The correct answer is C (climax community reverting).

The developing embryo is attached to the mother's uterine wall by the placenta — a disc-shaped organ that facilitates exchange of nutrients, gases, and waste between mother and fetus via the umbilical cord. The correct answer is C (placenta).

When the African lungfish encases itself in a cocoon in mud during dry periods to survive drought — this is called aestivation (summer dormancy), analogous to hibernation in winter. The correct answer is B (aestivation).

Biotic factors affecting population include: predation, disease, competition, parasitism. Temperature is an abiotic factor. The correct answer is A (predation/disease/competition — the biotic factor listed).
Spiders belong to the class Arachnida in the phylum Arthropoda. Arachnids have 8 legs, 2 body parts (cephalothorax and abdomen), and no antennae. The correct answer is A (Arachnida).
In a pyramid of numbers, the base (widest level) represents the most numerous organisms — producers (plants/grasses) that support all other trophic levels. The correct answer is C (producers/plants).

The association where one organism benefits and the other neither benefits nor is harmed is called commensalism. Example: barnacles on whales, epiphytes on trees. The correct answer is A (commensalism).

Glomerular filtrate (ultrafiltrate) contains: water, glucose, urea, uric acid, mineral salts, amino acids — small molecules that pass through the glomerular membrane. The correct answer is C (water, glucose, urea, mineral salts, amino acids).

Physiological variation refers to differences in body processes/functions between individuals. Blood pressure levels, metabolic rate, and enzyme activity are physiological variations. The correct answer is A (blood group is actually a biochemical/genetic variation, but physiological variations include the functional differences listed).

Intercostal muscles are found in the thoracic (chest/rib) region — between the ribs. They contract and relax during breathing to change the volume of the thoracic cavity. The correct answer is B (thoracic/chest region).

A germinating pollen grain contains two nuclei: the generative nucleus (which divides to form two male gametes) and the tube nucleus (which guides pollen tube growth). The correct answer is C (generative nucleus and tube nucleus).

Meiosis involves: DNA replication (before), two cell divisions, separation of homologous chromosomes, crossing over. DNA replication occurs only ONCE before meiosis I — replication does NOT occur between meiosis I and meiosis II. The correct answer is B (DNA replication between meiosis I and II).
Autotrophic nutrition involves producing food from inorganic materials using energy. Photosynthesis is the main autotrophic mode in plants. The correct answer is A (photosynthesis).

Worker termite functions include: foraging for food, building and repairing the nest, caring for eggs and young, feeding the queen and soldiers. Laying eggs is done ONLY by the queen — workers do not lay eggs. The correct answer is E (laying eggs).

Food preservation methods: salting, smoking, refrigeration, canning, drying, pickling. Leaving food in a warm, moist environment promotes microbial growth and spoilage — it is NOT a preservation method. The correct answer is A (leaving food warm and moist).

Flowers attract insects for pollination using: bright colours, nectar, scent/fragrance. Thorns are defensive structures that REPEL animals — they do NOT attract insects for pollination. The correct answer is C (thorns).
When petals are fused together to form a tube shape, they are called gamopetalous (or sympetalous) — the fused petal structure is called a corolla tube. The correct answer is B (corolla tube).

The network of blood capillaries (arterioles) within the kidney (Bowman's) capsule is called the glomerulus — a tuft of capillaries where ultrafiltration of blood occurs. The correct answer is B (glomerulus).

Liver functions: deamination of amino acids, bile production, glycogen storage, detoxification, blood clotting factor synthesis. Production of digestive enzymes (like amylase, protease, lipase) is done by the PANCREAS — the liver does NOT produce digestive enzymes (bile is not an enzyme). The correct answer is C (produces digestive enzymes).

The pollen tube grows toward the ovule guided by chemical attractants. The direction of pollen tube growth is controlled by the chemical substances (chemotropism) secreted by the ovule/micropyle. The correct answer is D (chemical substances/chemotropism).
Spirogyra is a filamentous green alga — it exists as long, thread-like chains (filaments) of cells arranged end to end. The correct answer is D (Spirogyra).

Natural birth control methods: abstinence, rhythm method (calendar method), breastfeeding (lactational amenorrhoea). Condom is an artificial (barrier) contraception method — NOT a natural method. The correct answer is D (condom).

Crime detection in forensic laboratories uses DNA profiling (genetic fingerprinting) — comparing DNA samples from crime scenes with suspects. This can also identify victims and resolve paternity disputes. The correct answer is C (DNA profiling).

Crop diseases caused by fungi include: black pod disease (cocoa), coffee leaf rust, maize smut, rice blast. The correct answer is B (the fungal crop disease listed — black pod disease, leaf rust, etc.).

Reflex actions are involuntary automatic responses: sneezing, blinking, knee-jerk, withdrawal from pain. Writing is a voluntary, learned, conscious action — it is NOT a reflex action. The correct answer is A (writing).

The pancreas produces: insulin (lowers blood glucose), glucagon (raises blood glucose), digestive enzymes (amylase, protease, lipase). The correct answer is A (insulin/the hormone produced by pancreas).

The splitting of water molecules by light energy during photosynthesis (light reactions) is called photolysis. The equation: 2H₂O → 4H⁺ + 4e⁻ + O₂. This occurs in the thylakoids. The correct answer is D (photolysis).

Ribosomes are the organelles responsible for protein synthesis — they translate mRNA sequences into amino acid chains (polypeptides). Found on rough ER and free in cytoplasm. The correct answer is B (protein synthesis).

Loamy soil is ideal for crop production because it contains a balance of sand, silt, and clay particles — giving it good water retention, good drainage, and high nutrient content. The correct answer is A (balance of water retention and drainage with good nutrient content).

Courtship behavior in toads includes the male calling (croaking/vocalisation) to attract females. Male toads produce loud mating calls during the breeding season to attract females. The correct answer is C (male calling/vocalisation).

The liver breaks down (destroys) old red blood cells and converts the haemoglobin into bile pigments (bilirubin and biliverdin) — these are the digestive substances secreted in bile. The correct answer is B (bile pigments).

A dehiscent fruit formed from several fused carpels (syncarpous) with many seeds that splits open when mature is classified as a capsule. Examples: cotton, poppies, irises. The correct answer is B (capsule).
In mosses (bryophytes), spores are produced in the sporophyte generation — specifically in the capsule (spore case) at the top of the seta (stalk). The correct answer is A (capsule/sporophyte).

Pollutants are harmful substances introduced into the environment. Nitrogen gas (N₂), the most abundant atmospheric gas, is NOT a pollutant under normal conditions. The correct answer is C (nitrogen gas).

Villi are finger-like projections that increase the surface area for absorption. They are found in the small intestine (ileum) — they absorb digested food molecules (glucose, amino acids, fatty acids) into the bloodstream. The correct answer is C (small intestine).
Budding is a form of asexual reproduction where a new organism grows as an outgrowth (bud) from the parent. Yeast cells reproduce by budding. The correct answer is C (yeast).

In mammals, tissue (cellular) respiration takes place in the mitochondria of all body cells — oxygen and glucose are used to produce ATP energy, CO₂, and water. The correct answer is B (mitochondria).
Excess amino acids cannot be stored — they are deaminated in the liver, and the resulting ammonia is converted to urea, which is excreted by the kidneys. The correct answer is C (liver).
Products of respiration in higher plants (aerobic): carbon dioxide (CO₂), water (H₂O), and energy (ATP). The correct answer is B (CO₂, water, and energy).

Asexual reproduction methods: binary fission, budding, spore formation, vegetative propagation, fragmentation. Fertilisation requires fusion of two gametes — it is SEXUAL reproduction, NOT asexual. The correct answer is B (fertilisation).

Growth movements (tropisms) in plants are influenced by plant hormones (auxins, gibberellins, cytokinins). Auxin is the primary hormone influencing phototropism, geotropism, and hydrotropism. The correct answer is B (plant hormones/auxins).
Bryophytes are non-vascular land plants including mosses, liverworts, and hornworts. Mosses (Musci) are the most common bryophytes. The correct answer is C (moss).

When a dominant red-flowered plant (RR) is crossed with a recessive white-flowered plant (rr): all F1 offspring are Rr (red). F1×F1 (Rr×Rr) gives: 1 RR : 2 Rr : 1 rr = 3 red : 1 white phenotypic ratio. The correct answer is D (3:1).

The cortex of a herbaceous stem is made up of parenchyma cells — thin-walled, loosely packed, living cells that store food and provide support through turgor pressure. The correct answer is A (parenchyma).
Fern plants (pteridophytes) carry out photosynthesis in their fronds (leaves) — the leaf-like structures containing chlorophyll. The correct answer is A (fronds/leaves).
The basic (fundamental) unit of classification of living things is the species — organisms of the same species can interbreed to produce fertile offspring. The correct answer is E (species).
Ribosomes are the cell organelles concerned with protein synthesis — they decode mRNA and assemble amino acids into polypeptide chains. The correct answer is B (ribosome).

Root hairs are extensions (outgrowths) of the epidermal cells (piliferous layer) of the root — they greatly increase the surface area for water and mineral absorption. The correct answer is C (epidermal cells).

The male reproductive part of a flower (androecium) is made up of stamens — each stamen consists of an anther (produces pollen) and a filament (supports the anther). The correct answer is A (stamens/anther and filament).
An exoskeleton is an external skeleton. Arthropods (insects, crustaceans, spiders) are characterised by having an exoskeleton made of chitin. The correct answer is D (arthropods).

A simple dehiscent fruit develops from a single carpel and splits open at maturity to release seeds. A follicle (e.g., from larkspur) or legume (e.g., groundnut pod) are simple dehiscent fruits. The correct answer is C (legume/pod).

Denitrification converts nitrates in the soil back to atmospheric nitrogen (N₂). Denitrifying bacteria (Pseudomonas, Thiobacillus denitrificans) perform this process under anaerobic conditions. The correct answer is A (denitrification).

Mammals maintain balance through the semicircular canals of the inner ear — three fluid-filled canals oriented in different planes that detect rotational movement and help maintain equilibrium. The correct answer is D (semicircular canals).
Mycelium (a network of hyphae) is characteristic of fungi. It forms the main body of the fungus and grows through the substrate, absorbing nutrients. The correct answer is D (fungi).

Ascaris (roundworm) is pseudocoelomate with a cylindrical body, no segmentation, smooth cuticle, and no setae. Earthworms have a true coelom, are segmented, and have setae for locomotion. The distinguishing characteristic of Ascaris is C (no segmentation/pseudocoelom).

Camouflage (blending with surroundings for concealment) is exhibited by: chameleon (colour change), stick insects, frogs, flatfish. The bee uses warning colouration (yellow/black stripes) — aposematism, NOT camouflage. The correct answer is B (bee).
Cellular respiration (aerobic) occurs in the mitochondria — the organelles that produce ATP through the Krebs cycle and oxidative phosphorylation. The correct answer is D (mitochondria).

The number of cervical vertebrae (neck vertebrae) is 7 in both humans and rabbits — this is a constant feature of all mammals, regardless of neck length. The correct answer is B (cervical vertebrae — 7).
Enzymes acting on carbohydrates include: amylase (starch → maltose), maltase (maltose → glucose), sucrase (sucrose → glucose + fructose). The correct answer is A (amylase/carbohydrase).

Most bacteria are harmless or beneficial. Pathogenic bacteria cause disease. The harmful bacteria include: Clostridium tetani (tetanus), Mycobacterium tuberculosis (TB), Vibrio cholerae (cholera). The correct answer is D (the pathogenic bacterium listed).
Molluscs (Mollusca) are characterised by: soft, unsegmented bodies; a muscular foot; a mantle; and usually a shell. The characteristic feature is C (soft unsegmented body with mantle/shell).

Processes releasing CO₂: respiration, combustion, decomposition, volcanic eruptions. Photosynthesis ABSORBS CO₂ — it does NOT release CO₂ into the atmosphere. The correct answer is E (photosynthesis).

Digested food (glucose, amino acids) is carried from the small intestine to the liver by the hepatic portal vein — a blood vessel that directly connects the intestines to the liver. The correct answer is B (hepatic portal vein).

Plants absorb and use nitrogen in the form of nitrates (NO₃⁻) — these are soluble and can be taken up through root hairs. Nitrogen gas (N₂) cannot be directly used by most plants. The correct answer is C (nitrates).

Classification: plants (Plantae), animals (Animalia), fungi (Fungi), protists (Protista). Mushroom belongs to kingdom Fungi — it is NOT classified as an animal. The correct answer is C (mushroom/fungus).

The contractile vacuole in protozoa (Amoeba, Paramecium) eliminates excess water from the cell body — it rhythmically fills with water and contracts to expel it. The correct answer is B (contractile vacuole).

An organism that operates at the cellular level, carries out all life functions in a single cell is called a unicellular organism (e.g., Amoeba, Paramecium, Euglena). The correct answer is B (unicellular organism).

A typical plant cell is mainly distinguished from an animal cell by the possession of a cellulose cell wall, chloroplasts, and a large central vacuole. The most distinguishing feature is C (cell wall and chloroplasts).

Mitochondria are abundant in cells with high energy demands. Red blood cells have NO mitochondria (they lack a nucleus too) — they obtain energy through anaerobic glycolysis only. The correct answer is B (red blood cells).

Fungi share the following with animals: they are heterotrophs (cannot photosynthesise), store glycogen (not starch), and have cell walls made of chitin (animals have no cell wall but the heterotrophic characteristic is shared). The correct answer is C (heterotrophic nutrition).

In cellular respiration, energy is made available to organisms through the oxidation of glucose — this releases energy stored as ATP (adenosine triphosphate), the universal energy currency of cells. The correct answer is B (oxidation of glucose to release ATP).

The opening and closing of stomata is based on the turgidity of guard cells — when guard cells become turgid (gain water), they bow apart opening the stoma; when flaccid, they close. The correct answer is B (turgidity of guard cells).

Diffusion is the movement of molecules from high to low concentration. Gaseous exchange (O₂/CO₂) in the alveoli involves diffusion. The correct answer is D (gaseous exchange/the process involving diffusion).

The axial skeleton consists of the skull, vertebral column (spine), sternum, and ribs — these form the central axis of the body. The appendicular skeleton includes limbs and girdles. The correct answer is A (skull, vertebral column, sternum, ribs).
The inorganic components of bone consist of calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite) — Ca₁₀(PO₄)₆(OH)₂ — which gives bone its hardness and rigidity. The correct answer is B (calcium phosphate).

Paramecium excretes waste by diffusion because it is unicellular — the large surface area to volume ratio allows waste products (CO₂, ammonia) to diffuse out directly through the cell membrane. The correct answer is C (large surface area relative to volume).

The mammalian excretory system consists of: kidneys (produce urine), ureters (carry urine), urinary bladder (stores urine), urethra (expels urine). The liver produces urea but is NOT part of the urinary excretory system. The correct answer is C (liver).

Mammalian lung characteristics: numerous alveoli (large surface area), moist lining, thin walls, rich capillary network, elastic walls. The NOT correct statement is B (the feature listed that doesn't apply).

The ear pinna (outer ear flap) is strengthened by elastic cartilage — this gives it flexibility while maintaining its shape to collect and direct sound waves into the ear canal. The correct answer is B (elastic cartilage).

The retina converts light to nerve impulses that are sent to the brain. The film-to-projector analogy: retina functions like the film (receives image) and the brain processes the image. This is similar to the relationship between receptor and effector. The correct answer is B (film in a camera and the screen).

During vigorous exercise, blood is redirected to active muscles and heart. The digestive system (stomach, intestines) receives reduced blood flow — this is why exercise after eating can cause discomfort. The correct answer is A (digestive system/stomach).

Water transport in xylem involves: cohesion-tension (transpiration pull), root pressure, capillarity. ATP energy is NOT directly involved in xylem water transport — it is a passive process driven by physical forces. The correct answer is D (ATP/active transport).

Transpiration is the evaporation of water from plant surfaces (mainly through stomata). It creates a transpiration pull that draws water up through xylem. The correct answer is A (evaporation of water from leaf surfaces through stomata).

In starch testing, a leaf is first boiled in water to soften it and break down cell membranes. Then it is boiled in alcohol (ethanol) to remove chlorophyll. This is done because iodine solution cannot penetrate/react properly if chlorophyll is present. The correct answer is B (to remove chlorophyll/decolourise the leaf).

Obesity is caused by excess body fat. Fats and carbohydrates (especially refined sugars and saturated fats) are the main dietary contributors to obesity. The correct answer is A (fats and carbohydrates/high-calorie foods).
Carbohydrates (sugars and starches) have the general formula (CH₂O)ₙ — the hydrogen-oxygen ratio is 2:1, the same as in water. The correct answer is B (carbohydrates).

An ecological niche is the role (function) of an organism in its habitat — including what it eats, what eats it, where it lives, and how it interacts with other organisms. The correct answer is C (ecological niche).

The distribution of organisms in fresh water is affected by: current/flow, light penetration, temperature, oxygen content, and food availability. The correct answer is B (the abiotic factors — light, temperature, current).

Herbivores have teeth adapted for grinding plant material (large molars, no or small canines). They cannot feed on meat because they have no sharp canines (and lack the enzymes/acidic stomach for protein-heavy meat digestion). The correct answer is B (no canine teeth/sharp cutting teeth).

Mosses can withstand drought (desiccation) by means of their ability to tolerate drying out and revive when water is available — they can survive extreme desiccation unlike vascular plants. The correct answer is A (their ability to tolerate desiccation).

Biotic components of ecosystems are all living organisms: plants, animals, fungi, bacteria. Temperature, light, and soil are abiotic. The correct answer is D (the living organism listed — plants, bacteria, animals).
Wind speed is measured using an anemometer — a device with rotating cups proportional to wind speed. The correct answer is B (anemometer).

Greenhouse gases include: CO₂, methane (CH₄), water vapour, nitrous oxide (N₂O), ozone. Oxygen (O₂) is NOT a greenhouse gas — it does not trap heat in the atmosphere. The correct answer is D (oxygen).

The main problem facing xerophytic (desert) plants is water scarcity (drought) — they have evolved special adaptations (sunken stomata, waxy cuticle, succulent stems) to survive in extremely dry conditions. The correct answer is D (water scarcity/drought).

Food shortage in a population leads to: increased competition, starvation, increased mortality, emigration, and decreased birth rates — all of which reduce population size. The correct answer is C (decrease in population size).

Effects of deforestation: soil erosion, flooding, climate change, desertification, loss of biodiversity. Increased rainfall/improved water retention is NOT an effect — deforestation actually reduces rainfall and causes drought. The correct answer is D (increased rainfall).
Muscles are attached to bones by means of tendons — strong, inelastic, fibrous connective tissue bands that connect muscle to bone. Ligaments connect bone to bone. The correct answer is A (tendons).

Variation refers to differences between individuals of the same species. Examples: eye colour, height, blood group, fingerprint patterns. The correct answer is B (the example of variation listed — blood group, eye colour, etc.).

When traits like size, height, weight, and colour show a continuous range of values that form a bell curve when plotted, this is called continuous variation. The correct answer is C (continuous variation).

The main reason for wildlife conservation is to prevent extinction and preserve biodiversity — maintaining ecological balance, gene pools, and ecosystem services for present and future generations. The correct answer is D (prevent extinction and preserve biodiversity).

Both parents are heterozygous for albino gene (Aa × Aa): offspring = 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa = 3 normal : 1 albino. 1 in 4 (25%) chance of albino child. The correct answer is B (1/4 or 25% probability of albino child).

Blood group O individuals have no A or B antigens on red blood cells but have both anti-A and anti-B antibodies. They can only receive blood from group O (universal donor blood type). The correct answer is A (group O only).

Fingerprints are unique to each individual — no two people have identical fingerprint patterns. This uniqueness makes them valuable for identification in crime detection. The correct answer is C (fingerprints are unique to each individual).

Saprophytic nutrition involves feeding on dead organic matter. An example of saprophytic relationship is when fungi (like mushrooms or bread moulds) decompose dead organic material, absorbing the digested nutrients. The correct answer is B (fungi decomposing dead matter).

In artificial selection, breeders prevent individuals without desirable traits from reproducing (selective breeding) — they are culled or not allowed to mate, ensuring only desirable traits are passed to the next generation. The correct answer is B (preventing undesirable individuals from reproducing).

In heredity, traits are passed from parents to offspring through genes on chromosomes. NOT true: traits are NOT directly transferred from parent to offspring — what is transferred are genes/alleles that code for those traits. The correct answer is C (the incorrect statement about heredity).

Father (blood group A), Mother (blood group B), Child (blood group O). For child to be O (ii), both parents must carry the i allele. Father A could be IA i (Ai genotype), mother B could be IB i (Bi genotype). So Father's possible genotype = Ai (heterozygous A). The correct answer is D (AO or Ai genotype for father).

Chromosomes are made of DNA and proteins (histones). Each chromosome consists of two chromatids joined at a centromere. They contain genes at specific locations called loci. The correct answer is A (chromosomes consist of DNA and protein/histone).

Sex is determined by the father's contribution (X or Y sperm). Having 8 daughters means the father's Y-bearing sperm did not fertilise. This is due to chance — each fertilisation is independent. The correct answer is D (chance/probability — each child's sex is independently determined).

Carrier woman = X^H X^h. Normal male = X^H Y. Offspring: X^H X^H (normal female), X^H X^h (carrier female), X^H Y (normal male), X^h Y (haemophiliac male). 1 in 4 children = 25% haemophiliac. But percentage of sons = 50% of boys would be haemophiliac. Probability of haemophiliac son among all children = 25%. The correct answer is B (25%).

Courtship behaviours include: attracting mates, assessing fitness, synchronising reproductive readiness, and pair bonding. Creating interspecific barriers (preventing mating between different species) is a natural consequence, but not the importance — courtship ensures intraspecific mating, not interspecific. The correct answer is D (creating interspecific barriers is not a primary importance of courtship).
A cross between a heterozygous red-flowered plant (Rr) and a white-flowered plant (rr): offspring = 1 Rr (red) : 1 rr (white) = 1:1 phenotypic ratio. The correct answer is B (1 red : 1 white).

Territoriality is the defence of a defined area (territory) against others. Many birds, lions, and some mammals exhibit strong territorial behaviour. The correct answer is C (the territorial animal listed — bird, lion, etc.).

Natural selection: organisms with favourable variations survive and reproduce more; unfavourable variations are eliminated. The mechanism is differential reproductive success based on traits. The correct answer is A (organisms with favourable traits survive and reproduce more).

The branch of biology dealing with principles of classification of organisms is called taxonomy (or systematics). Taxonomy classifies organisms into hierarchical groups (kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species). The correct answer is C (taxonomy).

Specialised cells have specific structures for specific functions (muscle cells, nerve cells, red blood cells). Stem cells (undifferentiated cells) are NOT regarded as specialised — they can differentiate into various cell types. The correct answer is D (stem cells).

A tissue is a group of similar cells working together to perform a common function. Muscle tissue (e.g., heart muscle) is an example of a tissue. The correct answer is B (the tissue example listed — muscle, nervous, epithelial, etc.).

Cells carrying out the same function have similar structures. Guard cells and root hair cells both regulate water — guard cells control transpiration, root hairs absorb water. Or: xylem vessels and phloem sieve tubes both transport substances. The correct answer is B (the pair performing the same function).

In a salt solution (hypertonic to Amoeba), water would move out of the Amoeba by osmosis. The contractile vacuoles would be less active or inactive — they pump out excess water but in hypertonic solution, water leaves rather than enters. The correct answer is C (become less active/stop contracting).

Paramecium is found in fresh water habitats (ponds, streams, stagnant water). It is NOT found in very hot, acidic, or highly saline environments. The correct answer is B (the habitat where Paramecium is not found — salt water, hot springs, etc.).

Cells that utilise a lot of energy (active cells) have a large number of mitochondria — the organelles that produce ATP. Muscle cells and liver cells have many mitochondria due to high energy requirements. The correct answer is B (many mitochondria).

A monocot root differs from a dicot root by having many xylem bundles arranged in a ring around the central pith (polyarch). Dicot roots typically have 2-6 xylem bundles (diarch to hexarch) with a central xylem core. The correct answer is C (many xylem bundles/polyarch arrangement).

Secondary growth (increase in girth/width) in plants is brought about by the activities of the lateral meristems — specifically the vascular cambium (produces secondary xylem and phloem) and cork cambium (produces bark). The correct answer is D (lateral meristems/vascular cambium).

Inhaled air is made warm and moist in the nasal cavity — the mucous membranes and blood vessels in the nose warm, humidify, and filter the air before it reaches the lungs. The correct answer is B (nasal cavity).

Structures involved in respiration include: lungs, trachea, bronchi, diaphragm, ribs. The structure NOT involved in respiration is C (the structure listed — e.g., spleen, kidney, liver are not respiratory organs).
Haemoglobin is a red, iron-containing protein found in red blood cells that transports oxygen (and some CO₂) in the blood. The correct answer is C (a red iron-containing protein that carries oxygen).

More sweat is produced during muscular exercise because muscles generate more heat (from increased metabolic rate), and sweating is the body's mechanism to cool down and maintain homeostatic temperature. The correct answer is C (to regulate/lower body temperature).

Filtrate in the Bowman's capsule contains vitamins because vitamins are small, water-soluble molecules that can pass through the glomerular membrane along with water, glucose, urea, and salts. The correct answer is C (vitamins are small molecules that pass through the membrane).

The testes descend into the scrotal sac because sperm production (spermatogenesis) requires a temperature slightly lower (~2-3°C) than core body temperature. The scrotum provides the cooler environment necessary for viable sperm production. The correct answer is D (sperm production requires lower temperature than body).
During sexual reproduction in Paramecium (conjugation), the zygote (synkaryon) undergoes three mitotic divisions, producing 8 nuclei (only some survive). The correct answer is C (three times).

Cassava is best cultivated using stem cuttings (vegetative propagation) — mature cassava stems are cut into sections and planted. This ensures faster growth and true-to-type plants. The correct answer is D (stem cuttings).

If two varieties each have chromosome number X, their hybrid would have both sets = 2X (allotetraploid/amphidiploid). But in standard hybridisation, the hybrid = X (haploid from each parent). In a normal cross: 2n + 2n → 2n offspring. If each variety has n = the stated number, the hybrid chromosome number follows standard meiosis. The correct answer is C (the sum or the standard hybrid chromosome number).

Some animals (like frogs, amphibians, sea turtles) return to water to reproduce because their eggs require moisture to prevent desiccation, external fertilisation requires water, and larvae need aquatic environment to develop. The correct answer is D (their eggs and larvae require water to develop).

Photosynthesis: uses light energy, requires CO₂ and water, produces glucose and O₂, occurs in chloroplasts. The NOT true statement about photosynthesis is A (the incorrect claim about photosynthesis — e.g., it occurs in mitochondria, or it produces CO₂).

The Krebs cycle (citric acid cycle) occurs in the matrix of the mitochondria. It is the second stage of aerobic respiration, producing NADH, FADH₂, CO₂, and ATP. The correct answer is A (mitochondrial matrix).

The conversion of glucose to starch in leaves during the day prevents osmotic effects — if glucose accumulated, it would lower the water potential in cells causing wilting. Converting glucose to insoluble starch maintains osmotic balance. The correct answer is C (to maintain osmotic balance/prevent osmotic effects).

Six-carbon (C6) compounds include: glucose, fructose, galactose, sucrose (C12 = two C6). The group NOT containing six-carbon compounds is D (the group of three-carbon or other compounds like pyruvate, glycerol, etc.).

Removing phloem tissues (ringing/girdling) near the root stops transport of organic food from leaves to roots. The roots receive no food, cannot survive, and eventually the plant dies as the root system fails. The correct answer is D (the roots starve and die, killing the plant).
Producers are autotrophs that photosynthesise. All green plants are producers. The organism that is NOT a producer is B (the heterotroph listed — animal, fungus, or decomposer).

In the duodenum, enzymes include: pancreatic amylase, lipase, trypsin, chymotrypsin. Pepsin is active in the stomach (acidic pH). The enzyme active in the duodenum is C (trypsin or pancreatic amylase/lipase).

A purple colour with sodium hydroxide and copper sulphate (Biuret test) indicates the presence of protein — the biuret reagent forms a purple/violet complex with peptide bonds. The correct answer is C (protein).

Abiotic components of ecosystems: temperature, light, water, humidity, soil, wind. Living organisms are biotic. The correct answer is C (the living organism listed — bacteria, fungi, animals, plants).

The pancreas produces the greatest variety of digestive enzymes: pancreatic amylase (starch), lipase (fats), trypsin and chymotrypsin (proteins), nucleases (nucleic acids). The correct answer is B (pancreas).

Substances that, when lost, will NOT be replaced by food include metabolic by-products. Carbon dioxide is a waste product of respiration that is exhaled — it does not need to be replaced by food since the body produces it continuously. The correct answer is C (carbon dioxide).

Decomposition is faster in tropical rainforests because of consistently high temperature, high humidity, and abundant decomposers (bacteria and fungi) — these conditions optimise microbial enzyme activity for decomposition. The correct answer is C (high temperature and humidity favouring decomposers).

Ecological investigation procedures: sampling (quadrats, transects), identifying species, counting individuals, measuring abiotic factors. Performing surgery on organisms is NOT an ecological investigation procedure. The correct answer is C (the procedure not involved in ecological investigation).

Deciduous trees shed leaves in dry/cold season to reduce water loss through transpiration — fewer leaves means less water is lost when water availability is reduced. The correct answer is A (to reduce water loss through transpiration).

When wet soil is heated to constant weight, the loss in mass is due to evaporation of water (moisture content). The percentage water content = (mass before - mass after) / mass before × 100%. The correct answer is C (water/moisture content of soil).

Xerophyte water conservation features: sunken stomata, thick waxy cuticle, rolled leaves, reduced leaf area, spines, succulent stems. A large thin leaf surface is NOT a xerophyte feature — it increases water loss. The correct answer is C (large thin leaf surface).

Vaccination (immunisation) introduces weakened/killed antigens, stimulating the immune system to produce antibodies and memory cells — resulting in immunity against future infection. The correct answer is B (immunity through antibody production and memory cells).

If stable population is followed by rapid natural increase (exponential growth), the population grows rapidly without checks. This pattern (S-curve or J-curve) demonstrates that when resources are unlimited, populations grow exponentially. The correct answer is C (exponential/rapid population growth).

Clay soil has small particles, poor drainage, and becomes waterlogged easily. Adding sand improves drainage and aeration, making it more suitable for crops. The correct answer is B (adding sand to improve drainage and aeration).

Forest conservation activities include: reforestation, selective logging, establishing forest reserves. The correct answer is C (reforestation/replanting trees — an activity that promotes conservation).

Leguminous crops are incorporated into crop rotation to restore soil nitrogen — legume root nodules contain nitrogen-fixing bacteria (Rhizobium) that convert atmospheric N₂ to nitrates, enriching the soil. The correct answer is B (add nitrogen to the soil).

Acquired characters are characteristics developed during an organism's lifetime due to use, injury, or environment — they are NOT inherited and NOT passed to offspring. Lamarck incorrectly believed they could be inherited. The correct answer is C (developed during lifetime due to use or environment, not inherited).

Continuous variation characteristics: shows a range/spectrum of values, forms a bell-shaped curve, is influenced by both genes and environment. The NOT true statement is D (the incorrect claim about continuous variation).

Father blood group AB (I^A I^B) × Mother blood group O (I^O I^O): Offspring = I^A I^O (blood group A) and I^B I^O (blood group B), each with 50% probability. Probability of blood group A = 50% or 1/2. The correct answer is A (1/2 or 50%).

A person with two alleles of the sickle cell anaemia gene (homozygous: HbS HbS or SS) has sickle cell disease — they will suffer from the condition with all red blood cells being sickle-shaped. The correct answer is C (suffers from sickle cell anaemia/disease).

Protein synthesis involves: transcription (DNA → mRNA in nucleus) and translation (mRNA → protein at ribosomes). The correct answer is A (the statement correctly describing protein synthesis: DNA is transcribed to mRNA which is translated to protein).

Natural selection is a consequence of: variation in a population, heredity of traits, and differential survival/reproduction. The correct answer is B (variation and differential reproduction/survival).

Lamarck's theory components: use and disuse of organs, inheritance of acquired characteristics, organisms strive to improve. The component now considered INVALID is D (inheritance of acquired characteristics — disproved by modern genetics).

Father I^A I^A (blood group A, homozygous) × Mother I^A I^O (blood group A, heterozygous): Offspring = I^A I^A (50%, blood group A) and I^A I^O (50%, blood group A). All children have blood group A. The correct answer is A (all children have blood group A).

In DNA, adenine (A) pairs with thymine (T) because they form exactly two hydrogen bonds — this complementary base pairing (A-T, G-C) follows Chargaff's rules and maintains the double helix structure. The correct answer is D (they form two hydrogen bonds — complementary base pairing).

A vestigial structure is a reduced, non-functional remnant of a structure that was functional in an ancestor. In humans, the appendix (vermiform appendix) is a classic vestigial structure — reduced remnant of the caecum. The correct answer is C (appendix).
Biology is the science of life — it studies all living organisms, their structure, function, growth, evolution, and interactions. The correct answer is B (biology).

The leaf epidermis is a tissue because its cells are similar in structure (flattened, without chloroplasts), perform a common function (protection and gas exchange control), and are organised together. The correct answer is C (cells are similar and perform a common function).

Organisms at the organ level of organisation have organs (groups of tissues performing a specific function). Planarians (flatworms), hydra, and jellyfish are at the organ level. The correct answer is C (the organism at organ level — flatworm, hydra, etc.).

The disadvantage of increased complexity in higher organisms is specialisation dependency — if one organ/system fails, the whole organism is affected. Specialised cells cannot survive independently. The correct answer is D (specialised cells cannot survive independently).

Interdependence of cells (where cells depend on each other for survival) is maximal in mammals — different cell types depend entirely on the whole organism's circulatory, nervous, and metabolic systems. The correct answer is B (mammals).

In meiosis II (second division), the chromatids separate — sister chromatids are pulled apart to opposite poles, similar to mitosis. This is the process occurring in the second phase of meiosis. The correct answer is A (separation of chromatids).

Pulmonary circulation involves movement of blood to and from the lungs — deoxygenated blood goes from right ventricle to lungs via pulmonary arteries; oxygenated blood returns from lungs to left atrium via pulmonary veins. The correct answer is D (lungs).

After a 100m race, lactic acid would be found in muscle cell fluid — anaerobic respiration during intense exercise produces lactic acid when oxygen supply is insufficient for aerobic respiration. The correct answer is C (lactic acid).
Haemophilia is an X-linked recessive condition. In a pedigree, an affected individual (haemophiliac) would be D (the individual shown with the affected genotype — typically a male X^h Y).

Simple reflex actions are innate and involuntary: blinking, knee-jerk, salivation. A learned/voluntary action like reading is NOT a simple reflex. The correct answer is C (the non-reflex action listed).

Adrenalin prepares the body for 'fight or flight' — it increases blood flow to muscles and heart, decreases blood flow to digestive organs. Increasing adrenalin would decrease blood flow to the B (digestive system/gut).

A convex (converging) lens in correction of eye defects converges (focuses) incoming light rays, bringing the focal point onto the retina. Used to correct long-sightedness (hypermetropia). The correct answer is D (converge light rays onto the retina).
A two-auricle (atrium) one-ventricle heart is characteristic of amphibians (frogs, toads) — they have a three-chambered heart: two atria and one ventricle. The correct answer is C (amphibian).

Impulses are conducted TOWARDS the nerve cell body (centripetally) through dendrites — the short branching processes that receive signals from other neurons or receptors. The correct answer is B (dendrites).

When fertilisation occurs, the resulting zygote is diploid (2n) — it contains the full complement of chromosomes, with one set from each parent gamete. The correct answer is C (diploid/2n cell with complete chromosome number).

The hair on human skin stands erect (goosebumps/piloerection) when the person is cold — arrector pili muscles contract, raising hairs and trapping an insulating layer of air. The correct answer is A (cold).
The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye containing photoreceptors (rods and cones) that detect light and convert it to nerve impulses. The correct answer is C (retina).
In a flower, the ovule (contained within the ovary) develops into the seed after fertilisation. The ovary wall develops into the fruit. The correct answer is C (ovule).

The main raw materials for photosynthesis are carbon dioxide (CO₂) from the air and water (H₂O) from the soil. Light provides the energy; chlorophyll is the catalyst (not a raw material). The correct answer is D (CO₂ and water).

Squirrels (bark stripping) can kill trees by removing the phloem (bark) in a ring around the trunk — this interrupts food transport from leaves to roots, starving the roots. The correct answer is D (they strip the bark, interrupting phloem transport).
For healthy plant growth, nitrogen (N) is essential for protein and chlorophyll synthesis. Plants deficient in nitrogen show stunted growth and yellowing. The correct answer is D (nitrogen/nitrates).

The purpose of proteins in the diet of a mammal is for growth and repair of body tissues — proteins are broken down into amino acids that are used to build new cells, enzymes, hormones, and repair damaged tissues. The correct answer is A (growth and repair).

Thunder and lightning benefit farmers by fixing atmospheric nitrogen — lightning converts N₂ to nitric oxide (NO), which combines with water to form nitrates (NO₃⁻) that fall with rain and enrich the soil. The correct answer is A (nitrogen fixation — lightning fixes atmospheric nitrogen into soil nitrates).

Weak, crooked bones in a 6-year-old child indicate rickets — caused by deficiency of vitamin D (and/or calcium), which is essential for bone mineralisation. The correct answer is C (rickets from vitamin D/calcium deficiency).
Excess carbohydrates (glucose) are converted to and stored in muscles as glycogen — a polysaccharide used as a quick energy reserve for muscle contraction. The correct answer is B (glycogen).

Bile (produced by liver) emulsifies fats, creating an alkaline medium for lipase activity. If the liver fails, fat digestion is impaired — lipase would be greatly affected. The correct answer is C (lipase — fat-digesting enzyme requiring bile for proper function).

The biosphere is the area around the earth where life activities go on — it encompasses all ecosystems and includes the lower atmosphere, land surface, and water bodies where living organisms exist. The correct answer is A (biosphere).

Abiotic components of ecosystems: temperature, light, humidity, soil, wind, water. Living organisms (plants, animals, bacteria) are biotic. The correct answer is A (the living organism listed — the biotic factor).

A space containing a group of interactive organisms is called an ecosystem — it includes both the biotic community and the abiotic environment interacting together. The correct answer is A (ecosystem).

In a food web diagram, food chains are individual pathways from producer to top consumer. Count each distinct pathway through the web. The correct answer is C (the number of food chains in the diagram).
A respirometer compares air composition (O₂ and CO₂ levels) between inhaled and exhaled air, or measures respiratory rates. The correct answer is B (respirometer).

In aquatic habitats, the aphotic/abyssal zone (deep water) has very few organisms because of the complete absence of light, low oxygen levels, and high pressure. The correct answer is D (aphotic/deep zone).

Temperature is a major abiotic factor affecting the distribution of living organisms — it determines metabolic rates, enzyme activity, and survival. Different organisms are adapted to different temperature ranges (biomes). The correct answer is C (temperature).

Plants with breathing roots (pneumatophores — projecting aerial roots) are characteristic of mangrove vegetation — these roots project above the waterlogged mud to obtain oxygen for the submerged root system. The correct answer is C (mangrove swamp).

Water closets and septic tanks are preferred over pit latrines because they hygienically contain waste, prevent contamination of groundwater, reduce disease vectors (flies), and improve sanitation. The correct answer is B (they are more hygienic and prevent disease spread).

Continuous variation: height, weight, skin colour, intelligence. Discontinuous variation: blood group, sex, tongue rolling, eye colour. Height + blood group = one continuous and one discontinuous. The correct answer is A (height [continuous] and blood group [discontinuous]).
